text:
Nashville is the better team on the underlying numbers, and the model has them scoring 3.31 goals tonight to San Jose's 3.00. The Predators create 2.53 expected goals per 60 and allow 3.00, while the Sharks sit at 2.35 for and 3.79 against, the leakiest defensive profile of the two by a wide margin. San Jose has been outplayed in every game of its last five by expected goals, with shares between 25 and 46 percent, which explains why a 3-6 home loss to Boston doesn't look like a fluke. Special teams tilt the same way. Nashville's penalty kill allows only 0.61 expected goals per game against San Jose's 1.05, and the Predators draw 4.0 penalties a game, so the Sharks will likely spend time shorthanded.

The goalie matchup is thin on evidence. San Jose's projected starter, Yaroslav Askarov, has a .850 save percentage and is 1.4 goals worse than expected this season, after a 19.4 goals-below-expected year across 47 games last season. Juuse Saros (projected) is at .900 and minus 0.38 this season, and was 10.19 below expected over 59 games last year. Neither is a stopper right now, but Askarov is the bigger concern.

Both teams are on one day of rest. Nashville has gone 3-1-1 over its last five, though it lost to Vegas 2-5 on Tuesday despite a 53 percent expected-goals share. For tonight, the model likes Steven Stamkos to score at 41 percent and Filip Forsberg at 38. For San Jose, Macklin Celebrini is the standout at 38 percent to score and 38 percent to record two or more points.
